In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AMM is a novel generative model for clustering and semi-supervised classification of complex data.
the AMM is a powerful tool for unsupervised clustering of complex data and can be used as a powerful tool for semi-supervised learning.
adversarially learned generative models can achieve state of the art results on unsupervised and semi-supervised data classification tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a generative model that can be used for semi-supervised clustering and classification of complex data.
the adversarial training allows the AMM to learn a better mixture model than the variational autoencoder (VAE) or the mixture density network (MDN) for clustering and semi-supervised classification.
we are the first to propose a generative model with adversarially trained latent variables that are continuous and categorical.
The main takeaway from our work is that

adversarial training can be used to learn the joint distribution between categorical and continuous latent variables, and this joint distribution can be used to cluster data without any labeled examples.
adversarially optimized generative models can be used for clustering and semi-supervised classification.
adversarial optimization of a generative model allows for the unsupervised discovery of semantic clusters in complex datasets.
